discussion_comments.comment_body:
> method name

Oh, yes. I originally had the check outside the routine. Will change name.

> Or how about doing the checks outside of the method?

I agree that would be tidier for the code and usage. However, I started that way, and multiple unit tests check whether `fs.existsSync` has been called and broke. I didn't think of an easy way of fixing the tests, other than moving the `fs. fs.existsSync` inside the routine. Then easy to completely bypass the new code and run the old tests.
We have several `_checkForX` routines already so following that style, `_checkForMissingExecutable`.
This method can start with an underscore to show it is private. (The older routines don't have an underscore, but you can see the convention with more recent `_excessArguments`.)

The high level check is that the settings are likely to work together. `Illegal` is too strong for my liking, and it is the combination rather than just `PassThroughOptions`. Suggest: `_checkForBrokenPassThrough`.

I didn't call `checkForUnknownOptions` here in my experiment in case not used in some branches, but in fact everywhere that `processAndAwaitArguments` is called, `checkForUnknownOptions` is the line before. So it is ok.

Actually, `processAndAwaitArguments()` was originally simply called `preprocess()`, but then I decided the unknown option check and argument processing were too unrelated to keep them in one function, and also I noticed that `checkForUnknownOptions()` was called without `_processArguments()` in one place, so I wanted to remove the `checkForUnknownOptions()` call from the function, but forgot to do it and ended up only renaming the function.

So we should either remove the `checkForUnknownOptions()` call from `processAndAwaitArguments()` as planned, or rename the function back to `preprocess()` or something along these lines and remove the redundant `checkForUnknownOptions()` calls. What do you prefer?

I prefer removing `checkForUnknownOptions` from `processAndAwaitArguments` too, not related enough so harder to understand what is being checked where.

(As understanding of the pattern evolves we might come up with a routine name where it makes sense included again!)

The name `getXXX` is a function to get something.

`this._actionHandler(getCheckedArguments());`.
For this code, it makes sense.

However, the code here does not use a return value.
I thought it was hard to understand what the 'get' was for.

Thanks. I'll take another look. I started without it and added it to make the "get" usage make more sense. I'll try separating out the check and the variadic support since that is only needed in one case.
So, if the method now accepts array of unknown options, that it should be named as `unknownOptions` etc.
So, if we change the function name, it'll be considered as breaking change, and should we deferred until the next major release.
